steps.title: Recover staged edits without ownership or capacity leaks
preconditions: Run the entire public tracer app -- test services atomic-batch command. Original source lines 1–274, 29 runtime callbacks and 29 HTTP requests remain unchanged. The appendix adds 45 HTTP requests for 74 total, within the unchanged 80-request cap.

Original real routes leave one pending typed-invalid-part manifest, two committed batches, and a failed-reference batch that should have been discarded. Add only one synthetic valid auth session for the existing member user in owned D1. No project-room draft/part/receipt state is seeded or read directly.

Both member auth sessions and the distinct team-owner session remain valid and entitled throughout. Manifest logical sessionId is preserved on replay; authorization session identity comes from its real bearer. There is no logout, entitlement lapse, epoch change, TTL wait or native device involved.

Fresh tiny one-part scene manifests keep room-wide count/byte budgets far below limits. Capacity probes are refused until the final probe is deliberately staged; original invalid-part draft and final probe remain pending until the owned temporary worker is disposed.

All document checks use public viewer snapshot/events. Equality excludes time-sensitive leases. Exact new scene data and event/receipt metadata are independently expected; no document tables, internal staging rows or receipt rows are inspected. Only users/sessions are compared through read-only D1 observations.

No live provider/authentication, actual image bytes, native UI, forced race/fault, crash/restart persistence, TTL/alarm execution, room-wide maximum, changed permissions or all manifest/part boundaries are claimed.
actions: Finish the original 29 requests, add one synthetic auth session for the existing member, and capture the five-item two-event baseline through viewer reads.

Prepare a first-session scene draft beside the original invalid-part draft. Refuse a second-session draft at per-user capacity; refuse correct-byte uploads from another user and another auth session, then accept the original-session upload.

Refuse a different-user takeover prepare. Refuse same-user/different-auth-session prepare and confirm the original draft no longer accepts parts. Prepare the second-session draft and refuse a third capacity probe.

Upload and commit the second-session scene. Validate exact receipt, authored snapshot addition and one snapshotRequired event. Recover its receipt from the first session; refuse changed-user/label replay and verify unchanged public state.
Re-stage the original missing-reference batch and upload it. Refuse a third capacity probe, then refuse its invalid-reference commit and verify unchanged snapshot/events.
Re-prepare the discarded first-session draft. Require batch_incomplete before re-upload; a third probe remains refused. Re-upload and commit once, validating exact scene/event addition.

Recover both accepted receipts through the second session with no extra changes. Fill the other slot with a probe, refuse a third draft, and reuse the original invalid-part manifest at capacity; invalid part and missing-part commit remain refused.
Preserve all original users/sessions plus exactly the added fixture session, five original document items and old events, empty R2, 74 HTTP checks and zero outbound.

expectations.description: The original invalid-part draft and a new first-session draft occupy both per-user slots. Preparing a second draft from another valid auth session of that same user returns exact 429/batch_capacity. Five quota refusals, interleaved with successful prepares/commits and cleanup, distinguish freed capacity from accidentally dropping unrelated staging. At the end a probe fills the other slot, a third draft is refused, and the original invalid-part manifest remains reusable at capacity but cannot commit without valid parts. No room-wide byte/count or expiry limit is tested.

An authorized different user and a second auth session of the same user cannot upload the first-session draft: both return exact 409/batch_session_changed. Original-session upload still succeeds. A different-user prepare returns command_reused without allowing takeover; same-user/different-auth-session prepare returns batch_session_changed and the old upload then reports batch_incomplete. Re-preparing that discarded draft later cannot commit until its part is uploaded again. Internal staging rows are not read.

After a cross-auth-session prepare refuses the first staged edit, its original-session upload is batch_incomplete. Re-preparing later yields batch_incomplete on commit until the same part is uploaded again, after which the scene commits once. This observes manifest/part disposal through public routes, not direct storage-row inspection.

A fully staged missing-reference batch is at user capacity as demonstrated by a third-draft refusal. Its commit returns exact 400/invalid_reference and leaves nonlease snapshot/full events unchanged. A fresh subsequent prepare succeeds, while a third probe is still refused, showing cleanup frees the failed draft slot without dropping the other pending draft.

A committed batch can be recovered by the other live auth session of the same user with the unchanged manifest, returning its exact original snapshotRequired receipt. Different-user and changed-label replays are exact 409/command_reused. Three successful receipt recoveries do not append events, change versions or add items.

The two successful one-part scene batches each add exactly one authored version-one scene and one snapshotRequired event with actor, label, request-bounded timestamp and sequential head. Epoch and timing stay unchanged; every prior item/event remains exact. Receipt items and event changes are empty by contract, so actual item content is checked in the fresh snapshot.

Wrong-user/session uploads of otherwise correct part bytes are refused before original-session upload succeeds. Later a typed-invalid direction part remains exact 400/direction_timing; its pending manifest is still reusable at capacity and commit is batch_incomplete. No part hash/size/JSON boundary or arbitrary replacement variant is newly claimed.

mappings.why: Session mismatch and semantic commit failure use targeted draft/part disposal. Public missing-part and capacity probes distinguish cleanup from stale uploaded-part resurrection; no raw table proof.
Stored accepted results are user/hash scoped rather than auth-session scoped; successful cross-session recovery and wrong-user/changed-label refusals exercise the public oracle.
Live route guards reach accepted-receipt lookup first; uncommitted staging then checks user/hash and rejects a different auth session with disposal. Entitlement/epoch change behavior is not varied.

Small sequential manifests reach the two-per-user staging boundary across two auth sessions. Successful prepare/refused third-draft probes track freed slots; global room budgets and alarm execution remain outside scope.

Re-prepared discarded staging cannot commit without uploaded parts; original typed-invalid staging also remains incomplete. Positive complete one-part manifests proceed; part-count boundary variants are not added.
Successful commit and targeted disposal yield one exact snapshot/event addition and recoverable receipt for each new scene. No storage fault or concurrent transaction is injected.

A real semantic APIError after attempted materialization rolls back visible document state and discards rejected staging; subsequent capacity probes and successful prepare distinguish release without dropping unrelated draft capacity.

Correct part bytes from an authorized other user or another same-user auth session are refused at staging ownership; original-session upload still succeeds. Body size and method variants are not exercised.

Valid one-scene content is accepted for its manifest, while the original typed-invalid direction payload fails validation and leaves no committable parts. New hash/size/syntax boundaries are not claimed.
Allowed uploads stage only transport parts; successful commits expose authored scene items once. Original and renewed first-session uploads are exercised without claiming byte-level table equality.
